subject: RE: Social Production Survey App
body:
Hi Sara,

 

I have spent most of the morning attempting to use the app as if I was a participant. There are a few more minor things I think should be refined for the demographic module some of which I can do myself with the researcher access (the rest I can summaries in a subsequent email). The mental health and community connection modules and quick and easy to use so all good there.

 

Unfortunately the Social Production module simply isn’t satisfactory.

 

• The first question that appears when I go into the social production app is ‘Which activity best describes how you spent this time? (what time? This sounds like a follow up question but it is the first question that appears and participants will be confused).

• This question lists activities to select from, asks you for a time period (which is confusing when I chose the work activity as the time period I entered was the whole period because I work every day (but then I had to go back and correct this when I understood I needed to choose a period of one day only).

• It then asked me where was I when I did this activity, who I was with, unpaid overtime, whether my profession was in the arts, then thanked me for my contribution to understanding mental wealth and directed me to submit (which seemed strange as it felt like the end of the survey).

• Only when I pressed submit button did a diary appear….and it didn’t default to the date that I had entered the activity for, I had to go looking for it. When I found the activity and was done editing the time period, it went back to the home page which meant I had to go back into the survey to enter the next activity (some people may not enter again thinking they may have completed the survey.

• On the diary page I can’t click on a time and have a selection of activities come up and modify the time by clicking and dragging like in a normal iphone diary.

• The whole experience was very complex, non-intuitive, and will frustrate participants, likely resulting in responses that will be incomplete and there will be high disengagement with the survey/app.

• Are you able to use the app as if you are a participant and see if the module works differently / is intuitive to use for you? I’m not sure whether something is wrong with the module, or the module just on my phone. Please note I am using an iPhone 8 with iOS 16.7.10.

 

Can we set up a meeting to discuss/reconfigure this module asap if it is indeed not just a problem with my phone app?

Many thanks,

Jo

Hi Jo,

Thanks a lot for your detailed feedback on the Social Production module. I'm sorry to hear about the challenges you've experienced. I will discuss it thoroughly with the team and keep you updated.

By the way, Amin is currently traveling for business, and his schedule is uncertain until October 23rd. However, I will try to arrange a meeting as soon as possible if needed. I will keep you posted.

On Friday, October 11, 2024 at 6:23:14 AM, Jo-An Occhipinti wrote:

Hi Sara,

 

I have spent most of the morning attempting to use the app as if I was a participant. There are a few more minor things I think should be refined for the demographic module some of which I can do myself with the researcher access (the rest I can summaries in a subsequent email). The mental health and community connection modules and quick and easy to use so all good there.

 

Unfortunately the Social Production module simply isn’t satisfactory.

 

• The first question that appears when I go into the social production app is ‘Which activity best describes how you spent this time? (what time? This sounds like a follow up question but it is the first question that appears and participants will be confused).

• This question lists activities to select from, asks you for a time period (which is confusing when I chose the work activity as the time period I entered was the whole period because I work every day (but then I had to go back and correct this when I understood I needed to choose a period of one day only).

• It then asked me where was I when I did this activity, who I was with, unpaid overtime, whether my profession was in the arts, then thanked me for my contribution to understanding mental wealth and directed me to submit (which seemed strange as it felt like the end of the survey).

• Only when I pressed submit button did a diary appear….and it didn’t default to the date that I had entered the activity for, I had to go looking for it. When I found the activity and was done editing the time period, it went back to the home page which meant I had to go back into the survey to enter the next activity (some people may not enter again thinking they may have completed the survey.

• On the diary page I can’t click on a time and have a selection of activities come up and modify the time by clicking and dragging like in a normal iphone diary.

• The whole experience was very complex, non-intuitive, and will frustrate participants, likely resulting in responses that will be incomplete and there will be high disengagement with the survey/app.

• Are you able to use the app as if you are a participant and see if the module works differently / is intuitive to use for you? I’m not sure whether something is wrong with the module, or the module just on my phone. Please note I am using an iPhone 8 with iOS 16.7.10.

 

Can we set up a meeting to discuss/reconfigure this module asap if it is indeed not just a problem with my phone app?

Many thanks,

Jo

subject: Social Production Survey App
body:
Hi Jo,


I hope all is well with you.


Thank you again for your comprehensive feedback on the Social Production module. I appreciate you taking the time to detail your experience. I have discussed your comments with the team and wanted to provide you with some insights for your reference. I will follow up in the other email thread to schedule our meeting so we can discuss these points further.


  1. First Question Confusion:

    • The content of the questions is based on the materials you previously shared and has been included to make the app testable for this phase. Please feel free to suggest more appropriate wording for the first question or any other changes you would like to see in the content of the other modules, and we will address them promptly.

  2. Time Period Selection:

    • We agree that the time period selection should offer clearer input based on your activity span. We’ll work on refining this and likely modify it to reflect the date when the activity is reported. We can discuss this further in our meeting.

  3. Survey Completion Misunderstanding:

    • We acknowledge that the premature "thank you" and submission prompt can be misleading. We’ll revisit this flow, remove the "thank you" page (see attached image), and change the "submit" button text to "report" on the final page. Please let us know if you have any additional suggestions.

  4. Diary Access and Navigation:

    • It’s essential that the diary defaults to the correct date. We will address this navigation issue to avoid unnecessary searching and streamline the process of adding activities. However, we’d like to discuss this item further in our meeting to ensure we align.

  5. Editing in the Diary:

    • We should delve deeper into this topic during our meeting and consider adding features that allow users to click on a time, select activities, and adjust times more intuitively, similar to standard calendar apps.

  6. Summary Report:

    • It would be beneficial to review how to calculate individual contributions to social production in more detail during the meeting.
Overall, we understand your concerns and agree that clarity and intuitiveness are crucial for participant engagement.

Thank you for your valuable feedback.

Best,

Sara
